P1: Async renames (DevForum PSA Jan 14 2026): Player:LoadCharacter -> LoadCharacterAsync; BadgeService:AwardBadge -> AwardBadgeAsync; MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> GetProductInfoAsync. Old names still work (informational deprecation, no removal scheduled), but new code should use the Async names. Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer were NOT renamed; keep using them as-is.
P2: Set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (Workspace properties, Server Authority section; released July 2026). It forces NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation on. Client-predicted gameplay logic goes in a callback registered with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn), so it can be re-simulated on rollback. Use time() as the clock inside it; tick(), os.time() and os.clock() do not roll back with the simulation.
P3: Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Timeline: opt-in from June 2026, planned default-on early 2027, property planned to be removed mid-2027 (then always on; Server Authority already forces it). At risk: code calling PlayerModule:GetControls() (Enable/Disable, move vectors), code relying on the old ContextActionService/UserInputService input-sinking behaviour against the default controls, and forked/modified copies of PlayerModule/ControlModule.
P4: With platform-integrated chat on, TextChatMessage.Text and .Translation return an empty string to experience code, so OnIncomingMessage/MessageReceived and Player.Chatted no longer give you message text (no reading text for custom filters, logs, or chat-parsed commands). Use TextChatCommand for admin/commands. Custom chat UIs must move to the TextChannelWindow-based customization rather than rendering message text themselves. Timeline: opt-in testing now through ~Feb 2027, default-on Feb 2027 (some wording says March), required ~May 2027.
P5: Limits are per experience (pooled across servers), per minute, scaled by concurrent users. Write budget = 300 + 20 x CCU per minute (some docs list 250 + 20 x CCU; design for the lower). Read = 300 + 40 x CCU, List = 300 + 2 x CCU, Remove = 300 + 40 x CCU. Storage = 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime unique players (compressed). Per key ~4 MB/min write; request size rounded up to the next KB. UpdateAsync counts as one read AND one write against the budgets.
P6: Because Gems are buyable with Robux, Gem-priced crates are paid random items (earnable Gems don't exempt them), and the Luck Potion is covered too. Before purchase, show every possible item with numeric odds totalling 100% (behind a clearly labelled Info/Odds button if long, not a bare icon). For the Luck Potion, show base and boosted odds numerically before buying it, and displayed odds must reflect the active boost. Drive both the roll and the display from one server odds table. Per player, on the server call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync and block paid crates where ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted is true (treat missing/errors as restricted, fail closed); gate trading of those items on IsPaidItemTradingAllowed == true. Re-check in each purchase/trade handler (not client-only); grant via ProcessReceipt.
P7: They are age-tiered account experiences: Roblox Kids (ages ~5-8) only sees experiences rated Minimal or Mild that are also in the curated selection; Roblox Select (ages ~9-15) sees up to Moderate plus selection; standard accounts are 16+. Selection excludes social hangouts, sensitive-issue and free-form drawing games by default; communication is off by default for Kids. Creator needs ID verification, 2-step verification and an active Roblox Plus subscription. Game needs a completed, accurate maturity & compliance questionnaire with an appropriate label (Minimal/Mild for Kids, up to Moderate for Select) and must meet the selection criteria.
P8: Creator Rewards Daily Engagement: 5 Robux per day for each Active Spender (>= $9.99 qualifying spend in the last 60 days) who plays your game 10+ minutes, when your game is among their first three launched that day. Paid as Earned Robux with a 60-day hold. DevEx: standard 0.0038 USD per Earned Robux; from June 8 2026 a US 18+ rate of 0.0054 USD for qualifying Earned Robux. Minimum cash-out 30,000 Earned Robux; legacy pre-Sept-2025 balances are exchanged first at 0.0035.
G1: Rules: (1) assign MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt exactly once in the whole game (a second assignment silently replaces the first). (2) Be idempotent per receipt.PurchaseId: store processed PurchaseIds in the same data document as the grant and write them together (UpdateAsync / session-locked profile). (3) Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. (4) Return NotProcessedYet if the player isn't in the server, data isn't loaded, or any save fails/errors (pcall); Roblox retries later (next join). (5) Never grant in PromptProductPurchaseFinished (fires on cancel too). Charged-but-nothing: returning Granted before/despite a failed save or when the player is gone. Double grants: no PurchaseId check on retries, the marker kept in a separate store from the grant (one write succeeds, the other fails), or granting in multiple places.
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever data could be written by more than one server/session or you read-modify-write (player data, counters, receipts, trades): it reads the current value and writes atomically with conflict retry, whereas GetAsync+SetAsync can overwrite newer data (rollbacks/dupes). SetAsync is only fine for blind overwrites of data nobody else writes. Transform rules: must not yield (no task.wait or other Async calls); may run multiple times, so no side effects and reset any flags on entry; return nil to cancel the write; return the new value; pass through userIds/metadata from keyInfo or they are wiped; check the session lock inside the transform.
G3:
Not safe. Bugs: NaN passes both comparisons (NaN < 0 and NaN > x are false); fractional or zero amounts pass; no rate limit or open-offer limit; and the gold isn't reserved, so the player can create many offers or spend the gold before the trade completes (double-spend/dupe). Fix: validate finite integer in range, escrow on the server, and re-validate atomically at completion.
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  if gold < 1 or gold > 1e9 then return end
  if not rateOk(player) or hasOpenOffer(player) then return end
  local g = player.Gold
  if gold > g.Value then return end
  g.Value -= gold            -- escrow (server-owned value)
  createOffer(player, gold)  -- refund on cancel; re-check at accept
end)
```
Keep authoritative currency in server data, not something the client can influence.
G4: The Animator writes Motor6D.Transform each frame for joints keyed by a playing track, after your Heartbeat write takes effect, so the aim is overwritten. Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (runs after animations are applied, before physics/render), composing with the animated value instead of replacing it: motor.Transform = aimCF * motor.Transform (or Transform * aim, or Lerp to fade). Beware compounding when no track keys the joint (keep a saved base and reapply, don't multiply last frame's result). Edit C0 (or C1) only for permanent or rare rest-pose changes like mount or grip offsets, not per-frame aiming; C0 replicates and moves the joint's rest frame that animations play relative to.
G5: The Animator blends per joint, and a track only affects joints it actually keys. Higher AnimationPriority wins (Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2-4); higher-priority tracks take their weight first and lower priorities only get the leftover (1 - sum of higher weights). Within one priority, weights are summed; if the total exceeds the remaining weight they are normalised (two same-priority tracks at weight 1 split 50/50 - the weak swing). Fix: set the swing to Action (or higher), weight 1 via Play(fade, 1)/AdjustWeight, walk stays Movement. Then on the arm the swing fully wins; weight 0.6 would give a 60/40 mix. Weight < 1 with nothing beneath blends toward the rest pose.
G6: Unit mismatch: Blender works in metres and the FBX exporter writes a unit-scale factor (centimetre-based), so the importer ends up multiplying by ~100. Recommended: set up the scene so 1 Blender unit = 1 stud (Unit Scale 1); apply rotation & scale (Ctrl+A) and put the root at the origin; FBX export with Apply Scalings = 'FBX Units Scale', Forward -Z / Up Y, Apply Unit; for rigs Add Leaf Bones off, Key All Bones on, Simplify 0. In the Studio 3D Importer check the Scale Unit (Studs). Or export glTF/GLB instead. Don't rescale rigs afterwards in Studio.
G7: The glTF/GLB exporter writes the base mesh data unless 'Apply Modifiers' is enabled, so the Mirror (other half) and Bevel never get exported. Fix: enable Include/Data > Apply Modifiers (export_apply=True), or apply the modifiers manually before export. Catch: Apply Modifiers doesn't work with shape keys (Blender can't apply modifiers to a mesh with shape keys, so shape keys/morphs are lost or the modifiers skipped), and for skinned rigs it would also bake the Armature modifier/pose, so keep it off for rigs; applied bevels also raise triangle count. For rigged or shape-keyed meshes apply Mirror/Bevel manually on a copy instead.
G8: Problem 1: fromScale(0.3,0.3) is 30% of width and 30% of height independently, so on screens with different aspect ratios the frame's shape changes. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (e.g. AspectRatio 1, DominantAxis), optionally UISizeConstraint/UIScale for min/max sizes; scale for position. Problem 2: the button sits where the notch/cutout and the Roblox top bar draw. Fix: keep interactive UI in a ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets (default; avoids top bar and notch) and SafeAreaCompatibility = None, offset using GuiService.TopbarInset if aligning beside the top bar; don't set ScreenInsets = None / IgnoreGuiInset on interactive HUDs. Put full-bleed decoration in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None.

```lua
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {price=..., maxQty=...}
local remote = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local last = {}

remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  local now = os.clock()
  if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.25 then return end
  last[player] = now
  if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 64 then return end
  if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  local item = Items[itemId]
  if not item or quantity < 1 or quantity > (item.maxQty or 99) then return end
  local data = PlayerData.get(player)  -- server-owned, loaded
  if not data then return end
  local cost = item.price * quantity   -- price from server, never client
  if data.Coins < cost then return end
  data.Coins -= cost
  data.Inventory[itemId] = (data.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
  PlayerData.markDirty(player)
end)
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Price and balance live on the server; the client only sends intent.

```lua
-- key "u_"..userId ; doc = {data=..., lock={jobId=, t=}, receipts={}}
local LEASE = 90
function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 6 do
    local ok, doc = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(d)
      d = d or newDoc()
      if d.lock and d.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - d.lock.t < LEASE then
        return nil               -- locked by another server: cancel write
      end
      d.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()}
      return d
    end)
    if ok and doc and doc.lock and doc.lock.jobId == game.JobId then return doc end
    task.wait(0.5 + attempt * 0.4)  -- old server (teleport/rejoin) still releasing
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, please rejoin")  -- never play on default data
end
function save(player, release)
  store:UpdateAsync(key(player), function(d)
    if not d or not d.lock or d.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't write
    d.data = cache[player]
    d.lock = (not release) and {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()} or nil
    return d
  end)
end
-- autosave + renew lease every ~30s; save(p, true) on PlayerRemoving and before TeleportAsync;
-- BindToClose: save+release all in parallel, wait (<30s). Receipts idempotent by PurchaseId in the doc.
```
Or use ProfileStore, which implements this.

T4: On the client, FireServer automatically passes the sending player as the first argument to OnServerEvent. By passing LocalPlayer yourself, the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50), so `amount` is the Player Instance and amount + 1 errors. Fix: client `remote:FireServer(50)`; server `function(player, amount)`. Then validate on the server: `if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end` plus a range check; never let the client say who the player is - always use the injected `player`.

In Studio solo play the player can join before (or while) the server Script starts, so Players.PlayerAdded has already fired before your Connect and is missed. (Live servers usually run scripts before anyone joins.) Standard fix: connect, then also handle players already present:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player) --[[create leaderstats]] end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Also avoid yielding (WaitForChild, slow requires, DataStore calls) before the Connect.

```lua
local BadgeService = game:GetService("BadgeService")
local BADGE_ID = 123456

local function awardObbyBadge(player: Player): boolean
  local ok, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
  if ok and has then return true end
```

T8: RenderFidelity is not scriptable at runtime: it is only honoured when set in Studio before publishing, so script writes (or changing it in a running game) do nothing. Precise only disables that mesh's own fidelity reduction; other systems still drop detail at distance in live clients: the device's graphics quality level and memory-pressure LOD on weaker devices, and with StreamingEnabled the Model.LevelOfDetail (StreamingMesh/Automatic) swaps distant models for low-detail impostor meshes. Fix: set Precise in Studio and republish, set the hero Model's LevelOfDetail = Disabled (ModelStreamingMode Atomic/Persistent if needed), and test at realistic graphics quality. Use Precise sparingly (performance cost).
